title: Game test
description: The result of one run of a game test, by the agent or by the replay script an agent left. Which game it ran against is stored beside the document, not in it.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema the document follows. Version 1 had no mode: its tests were played in demo mode. Version 2 had no runner: the agent ran all its tests.

mode.description: Which account the test played with, and so what it checked.

oneOf.description: An account with balance: the game launches in real-money mode and one round is played for real money at the minimum stake.
An account without balance: the game launches in real-money mode, and trying to bet shows that the balance is not enough.

runner.description: What drove the browser. testson sets it, not the agent.

oneOf.description: An AI agent tested the game and reported what it found.
testson replayed, without an agent, the script an earlier agent run left for this version of the game.

script_id.description: The number of the script that was replayed. Present only when the runner is 'script'.

script_outcome.description: How far the replay got. Present only when the runner is 'script'.

oneOf.description: Every step of the script ran, so the status is a verdict on the game.
A step of the script could not run: the script no longer fits the game, and the agent tests it again.
A step after the spin could not run, so the round was played but not checked. The script is retired, and the agent tests the game at a later test, not right away, so as not to play another round.
The game loaded a build.js with another ETag than the one the script was written for, so the replay stopped before betting and the agent tests it again.
A check of the account or the stake stopped the replay before betting, such as an expired session or a stake above 1 €. The agent would be stopped the same way.

status.description: What the run found out about the game.

oneOf.description: The game works: every step ran and the game behaved as expected in all of them.
The game is failing: a step ran against the game and what it checked did not hold.

The test itself failed: it could not be completed for a reason that is not the behaviour of the game, such as the browser not starting or the page never loading, so the run says nothing about the game.

summary.description: One or two sentences on what was tested and why the run got its status.

game_url.description: URL of the game, or of the page it was launched from.

duration_ms.description: Total duration of the test in milliseconds.

balance_before.description: Account balance shown before the first bet was tried, as written on the page, such as '12,40 €'.

balance_after.description: Account balance shown once the round settled or the bet was refused, as written on the page.

video_path.description: URL path the session recording is served at, such as '/data/...'. Absent if the browser never started.

trace_path.description: No longer written: the trace records the login session, so it stays private and is never served. Older documents may still hold it.

post_messages.description: Messages the windows of the page posted to each other, such as the lobby and the game client, in the order they were received.

steps.description: The timeline of the test: every step it is made of, in execution order, with the evidence captured during it.

error.description: Why the test could not be completed. Present only when the status is 'test_failed'.

game_version.description: Which build of the game client the test was run on: the ETag the server of the provider sends with its build.js, as testson read it before the run, or as the browser loaded it when testson could not.

build_url.description: URL of the build.js of the game client, without its query string.

etag.description: ETag response header of build.js, as sent, quotes included.

post_message.description: One message a window of the page posted to another, with whatever looks like a token redacted.

oneOf.description: The lobby page received it, usually from the game client.
A frame of the page, usually the game client, received it.

origin.description: Origin of the window that posted it.

frame_url.description: URL of the window that received it, without its query string.

step.description: One thing the test does or checks, its outcome and the evidence captured during it.

action.description: Playwright action the step performed, such as 'goto', 'click', 'press' or 'expect'.

description.description: What the step does or checks, in words a person who does not know the test can follow.

selector.description: Locator the action targeted, if any.

oneOf.description: The step ran and what it did or checked held.
The step ran and did not hold. It is the step the test stopped at.
The step never ran, because an earlier step failed, or it was an optional step of a replay script and what it handles did not show.

screenshots.description: Screenshots taken during this step, in chronological order.

console_messages.description: Warnings and errors written to the browser console during this step.

failed_requests.description: Network requests that failed or returned an HTTP error status during this step.

screenshot.description: One image captured during a step.

path.description: URL path the image is served at, such as '/data/...'.

console_message.description: One message written to the browser console.

source_url.description: URL of the script or page that produced the message.

failed_request.description: One network request that did not succeed.

status_code.description: HTTP error status returned. Absent if no response was received.

error.description: An error raised during the test.

environment.description: Browser configuration the test ran with.

viewport.description: Size of the browser viewport in pixels.

user_agent.description: User agent string the browser sent.
